halves_read: Both halves are in one repo: the game client and server source (src/, lib/, 3rdparty/) and the data pack (data/). Only the data half was read in depth here: data/base/stats (JSON balance tables), data/base/audio (audio.json and file counts), data/base/structs and data/base/effects (PIE model headers, file names), data/mp (multiplayer maps and components), and the licence files (COPYING, COPYING.README, COPYING.NONGPL, README.md, .gitmodules). Source code was not read beyond the licence headers.
code_licence: GPL-2.0-or-later. README.md line 300 states the project is free software under GPL; COPYING.README line 14 says 'Everything included (source code and data)' is GPL version 2 or later, except the music and video not included. Third-party code under 3rdparty/ has its own licences (MIT, BSD, Boost, MPL 2.0, ISC, CC0 for expected; see COPYING.NONGPL).
asset_licence: Mixed, file by file. COPYING.README line 14 and line 15 sets the default as GPL-2 or later for included data. COPYING.NONGPL lists the exceptions: CC0 (some maps and images), CC BY-SA 3.0 (some textures, wheel models, a campaign banner, one multiplayer map), CC BY 4.0 (Font Awesome replay icons), MIT (flag images and Bootstrap UI icons, AMD FSR and SMAA shaders), OFL 1.1 (a CJK font, not in box). Music and video are not in the box (COPYING.README line 15; README.md line 38; data/music is an empty submodule).
rights_holder_status: Original game released by Eidos with Pumpkin Studios (README.md lines 34 and 37 name Pumpkin Studios and Eidos). COPYING.README line 43 grants permission to use the name, logos, stories and texts. Individual artists are credited in COPYING.NONGPL for listed files. The rights position for the remaining game art, audio and music is not stated beyond the GPL default and the per-file list. Treat as released-source, not clean-room.

inspiration: Weapon effect against movement class is one table: each weapon effect has a percentage per propulsion class (tracked, wheeled, legged, hover, lift, half-tracked, propellor). Some effects are flat, which is a deliberate choice (data/base/stats/weaponmodifier.json lines 11 and 38). Recreate: a damage-type by target-class grid for our creature classes and armour types, with flat rows for special damage.

Surface speed is a table per terrain type with a speed factor for each locomotion class (data/base/stats/terraintable.json lines 4 and 5). Recreate: each ground type sets a speed multiplier per creature locomotion (swim, fly, burrow, walk); our biome tags use the same shape.

Sound events are rows with a file name, a loop flag, a range in world units (the file says 128 units equal one tile) and a volume from 0 to 100 (data/base/audio/audio.json line 3). Recreate: our combat cues as rows with range and volume so the impact sound falls off with distance (row 12).

Effects such as blood, dust, explosion and smoke are small models stored in the same text mesh format as units (data/base/effects/fxblood.pie, fxdust.pie, fxdirt.pie, fxexpdrt.pie; file names only, not opened). Recreate: blood and dust as short-lived particle sprites in our palette, driven by one effect table (row 8).

Units are assembled from separate body, locomotion and weapon parts (data/base/components/bodies, prop, weapons). Recreate: our hero gear as layered parts on one rig (row 15), so a new weapon is a new part, not a new model.
Structures and features reuse one texture page per model (structs/miuptrim.pie line 3). Recreate as a shared atlas per zone for props, to keep draw calls low.

briefs.label: Duel grid of damage types
briefs.why: A small effect-by-class grid gives every damage type a clear strength and weakness that a player can learn in one fight.
briefs.keep: Damage types as rows; target classes as columns; percentage per cell; a flat row for the special case.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy: our armour and creature classes, our damage names, a colour grid readable at 375 wide, and no shared numbers.

briefs.label: Ground speed card
briefs.why: A surface that slows heavy creatures but not swimmers makes terrain matter without a new mechanic.
briefs.keep: Surface type with a speed multiplier per locomotion class.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original: our biome tags (bog, ash, ice) and our locomotion classes; swimmers gain on water and bog, not on ice.

briefs.label: Blood as a small effect model
briefs.why: A short, distinct blood burst reads as a hit at phone size and costs little to draw.
briefs.keep: Blood as a separate short-lived effect in the same content pipeline as models.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original: a fan of droplets as 2D sprites in our palette, colour by wound level, no copy of the original shape.

briefs.label: Three-part hero build
briefs.why: Swapping body, locomotion and weapon parts gives many builds from few parts.
briefs.keep: Units assembled from separate body, locomotion and weapon parts.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original: our hero rig with armour plates, cape and weapon as layers; no unit body copy.

briefs.label: Range-scaled combat cue
briefs.why: A sound with a world-unit range and a loop flag falls off with distance, so a fight sounds closer or further by the camera.
briefs.keep: Event rows with file, loop flag, range and volume.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original: our three-layer hit cue, range in our own arena units, and a stinger on kill.
